Using Interjections & Expressions to React and Comment on a Story

When you listen to a story, it is always important to react and comment on it. You do this by using interjections or phrases to express emotion. Here are some common ones and examples of their use in conversations:

A: Hey, what happened?
B: You won't believe this. There's a leak announcing a huge layoff.
A: Uh-oh! This is not good.

A: The company decided to fire more than 300 employees.
B: Oh my gosh! I can't believe it!

A: No wonder, he's been so quiet.
B: Wow! This is insane!
A: That's typical of him.

The Present Perfect is a combination of the Present tense and the Perfect aspect.
The tense demonstrates the position of an event or action in time. In the Present Perfect, you use a past tense (past participle) because the action happened at a time in the past.
The aspect refers to how you should view the event in relation to time (in other words the perspective ). In the Present Perfect, you use a Perfect aspect - the event has a connection to the present time.
The Present Perfect is used to express a past event that has present consequences.

1. Using the Present Perfect

1. Indefinite time before now: We use the Present Perfect to describe an action that happened in the past but we don't know exactly when. The time is NOT important.
      • There's been a leak on social media.
      • He's planned a layoff that will affect the company.

Remember: You must not use any time expressions such as yesterday, last week, two months ago.
      • There has been a leak on social media yesterday.

1. Recent past action:The Present Perfect is also used to talk about a recent past action. We normally use “just”.
      • This news has just come out.

1. Experiences:The Present Perfect describes experiences a person has had or hasn't had. We normally use the expression “Have you ever + past participle” to ask about people's experiences.
      • “Have you ever used Chirp?”

Janet: Hi Miranda, what's wrong?
Miranda: You won't believe this. Have you used the social media website Chirp? There's been a leak from an employee at Holly's.
Janet: Uh-oh. This sounds serious ...
Miranda: This explains why Farmani has been reluctant to discuss training and personnel needs.
Janet: Go on.
Miranda: The word is out that he has planned a massive layoff of employees.
Janet: Oh my gosh! What was he thinking? Has he considered the impact this could have on his brand?

Miranda: Not only that, this leak has come out just before our major publicity event. This will hit the press immediately.
Janet: I can't believe it!
Miranda: Believe it. There'll be demonstrations at the event.
Janet: Wow. This is insane. Let's calm down for a minute and think. Publicity event or not, this action will damage his firm's reputation.
Miranda: No wonder he's been so silent.
Janet: That's typical of him. But hear me out. Perhaps, if we move quickly, this is just the right timing.

Miranda: How is that?
Janet: A huge layoff is bad press at any time. But Farmani may be convinced of the seriousness with the timing of our PR event.
Miranda: Ah ... I never thought of that.
Janet: I'll give him a call and convince him to make an announcement we'll publicize at the event. It could be the perfect time to rebrand. I'll urge him to consider retraining his employees rather than hiring new people.
Miranda: Brilliant!
